subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline controls be added through shared `MessagePresentation` typed actions and an authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, and should any WebChat capability/config key be introduced despite retired WebChat config?
rationale: The first implementation defines public Gateway/UI interaction semantics, callback security, and possibly a new config surface, so automation should not choose that product and security boundary.

options.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
options.body: Use shared typed presentation actions, add a scoped authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, keep webhook routing out of v1, and make an explicit yes/no decision on WebChat capability config.

options.title: Protocol first, UI second
options.body: Approve only the schema/RPC/auth contract first and leave Control UI rendering and click-state behavior for a follow-up item.

options.title: Defer interactive WebChat
options.body: Keep WebChat text-only for now and route richer reactions, feedback, and approval-card UX through a later WebUI interaction direction.

recommendation.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
recommendation.body: Use shared typed presentation actions, add a scoped authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, keep webhook routing out of v1, and make an explicit yes/no decision on WebChat capability config.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across WebChat config retirement and the shared presentation action contract.
